findings.title: SC 10's "its other metrics are unchanged" clause has no corresponding test step
findings.description: Success Criterion 10 (slice design, line 278) reads: "…gets `duplicated_lines` as `tool_failed` with a WARNING naming the count and the ceiling, **and its other metrics are unchanged.** A test lowers the constant to trigger it." Task 11 (bullet at the cited line) tests the tool_failed outcome and WARNING at the `measure_duplication` module level, where "other metrics" don't exist; Tasks 13 and 15 exercise the adapters but not the ceiling scenario. The failure-mode table's second row likewise ends with "Other metrics are unaffected", and the Technical Requirement says "Failure-mode tests assert both the signal and the outcome for each row" — so this clause of row 2 is left unmet by name. The structural separation (D1: duplication is its own pass returning one measurement) makes the risk low, but the criterion explicitly asks for the assertion. Cheapest fix: add one bullet to Task 13 — with `DUPLICATION_MAX_TOKENS` patched small, assert through `PythonAdapter` that `duplicated_lines` is `tool_failed` and file/function length and lint are identical to an unpatched run (and mirror it in Task 15 for TypeScript, since SC 10 says "a language", not "Python").

findings.title: No load-test task exists, and none is required here
findings.description: The slice restates one resource bound — the D3 memory estimate (133 bytes/token, ~530 MiB at 4M tokens) — but the design discharges it as an enforced ceiling (`DUPLICATION_MAX_TOKENS`) that converts the overload into an explicit `tool_failed` absence, tested by lowering the constant (SC 10, Task 11) rather than by generating a multi-gigabyte corpus. The repository has no `tests/load/` convention (slice 400 introduced none), and adding one would be scope creep. Recording this so the omission is read as a deliberate design choice, not a gap.

findings.title: Task 10 is the largest task (Effort 4) but is correctly left unsplit
findings.description: Task 10 (the window pass: id mapping, rolling hash with collision confirmation, overlap rule, ceiling, `counting` text) is the algorithmic core and carries the module's ~300-line budget on its own. Splitting it (e.g. hash step vs. window index) would create an intermediate state that can't be tested end-to-end; the spec is exhaustive and each sub-bullet is independently verifiable, and the hash step is already isolated for collision testing. At the other end, no task is too granular — the Effort 1 tasks (1, 17, 28, 30) are each single-commit units.
